post_title: How many AIS-visible commercial ships will the hormuz.now tracker count crossing the Strait of Hormuz on October 29, 2026?

question.title: How many AIS-visible commercial ships will the hormuz.now tracker count crossing the Strait of Hormuz on October 29, 2026?
question.description:
hormuz.now is a tracker of ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz during the 2026 Hormuz crisis, which it dates from 28 February 2026 (US and Israeli strikes on Iran), with the IRGC confirming a closure on 2 March 2026. As of mid-October 2026 the site's live status label is "Restricted": AIS-visible commercial traffic is running at roughly 10% of normal — about 9–10 ships per day over the trailing week, against a pre-crisis baseline of about 84.8 per day. Ships are reported crossing under US naval coordination while Iran claims control and requires transit permits.

The tracker counts distinct AIS-visible commercial ship crossings per UTC day using a published methodology. Because it relies on AIS (Automatic Identification System) transponder data, it misses ships transiting with their transponders switched off — and many do during the crisis. Other trackers report higher numbers: on 27 September 2026 IMF PortWatch (AIS-only) recorded 1 transit while Windward (combining AIS with satellite data) counted 24, 14 of them "dark". So hormuz.now's AIS-visible counts can undercount real traffic substantially, and PortWatch's own figures run even lower and are published with a multi-week lag.

Recent daily AIS-visible counts reported by hormuz.now (UTC days): 1 Oct = 1, 9 Oct = ~12, 10 Oct = 6, 11 Oct = 8, 12 Oct = 7, 13 Oct = 10, 14 Oct = 10. Single-day counts are noisy and depend on ship scheduling, convoy coordination under naval escort, and how many vessels keep transponders on. hormuz.now publishes a dated archive page for each day at https://hormuz.now/traffic/<YYYY-MM-DD> giving that day's total, plus downloadable data at https://hormuz.now/data.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the number of AIS-visible commercial ship crossings of the Strait of Hormuz recorded by the hormuz.now tracker for the full UTC day of 29 October 2026, as reported on that day's archive page at https://hormuz.now/traffic/2026-10-29 (the figure stated as "[N] AIS-visible commercial ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz"). For example, if the page states "8 AIS-visible commercial ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz", this resolves as 8. The figure must be read only once the day is complete — i.e. after the page drops any "still in progress" / live notice and shows the finalized total for 29 October 2026.
question.fine_print: The count is the single daily total of distinct AIS-visible commercial ship crossings for 29 October 2026 (UTC) as defined by hormuz.now's published methodology at https://hormuz.now/methodology, which counts ships whose AIS transponders are on and therefore excludes vessels transiting "dark" (AIS off). If the figure on the archive page and the figure in the downloadable CSV/JSON at https://hormuz.now/data differ for the finalized 29 October 2026 count, the archive page figure at https://hormuz.now/traffic/2026-10-29 is the canonical value. If the per-day page is temporarily unavailable or not yet finalized, resolution waits until hormuz.now publishes the finalized count for 29 October 2026. If hormuz.now permanently ceases to publish this figure before a finalized 29 October 2026 count is available, the question is annulled.
